LESSON: SIGN READING 5.3.3 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Sign Reading 5.3.3 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 5.3.3 Comprehension, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we show that we have understood what we have read? 2. How can we predict how a story, poem or conversation will end?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 5.3.3 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: speaking or signing skills as learners retell the story in their own words.

Values:
Unity: The learner’s cooperation skills are enhanced as the learner participates in answering indirect questions with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skill: Effective communication as learners answer comprehension questions correctly

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learner relates Sign reading for comprehension to their learning in Mathematical activities, Environmental activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted course books, Chart, class readers, course books, flash cards, recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, dictionary, internet, signed audio- visual recordings
